Operation Brevity: your first Operations Stage, step by step

Every move, roll and calculation for both sides, with the rule case or chart each number comes from. Read the three lanes left to right, top to bottom. The checklist on the left ticks itself off as you scroll.

How to read this

  • Allies lane: what the British/Commonwealth players do.
  • Axis lane: what the German/Italian players do, including reactions and defensive choices.
  • Why lane: the reasoning behind the decision.
  • ⚡ amber bars mark moments when the other side may respond.
  • Grey chips 📖 name the rule case or chart. Code-style boxes show the arithmetic.

Dice are read as two digits: first die tens, second die units (3 then 6 = 36).

Assumptions we made

  1. Allies are Player A and move first (the scenario skips initiative).
  2. 2 RflBde and I/62 are played as foot infantry (CPA 10).
  3. The 57th Artillery = 6 × 75/18, 3 × 100/17 and 2 heavy AA 75/46, per the OA chart.
  4. The 75/46's bracketed Anti-Armor (5) is usable when no other unit in the hex has a plain rating.
  5. The unfinished coast road costs the same as clear terrain (2 CP, 4 BP).
  6. Hexside terrain shifts apply only when every attacking unit crosses that hexside.
  7. Every die roll is invented for the tutorial. In your game, roll for real and use the same tables.

Why

Why this setup

The Allied hexes are fixed by the scenario. The Axis puts one unit in each of the four victory hexes (the scenario demands Halfaya, Sollum and Capuzzo; Bardia is required for II/62) and keeps every fast unit in one reserve stack, one hex from Capuzzo, ready to counterattack whatever the British take.
Step 2

Bookkeeping & who goes first

Allies

Allies are Player A

The scenario skips the Initiative step, so we agree the attacker moves first. The Allies run their whole Movement & Combat Phase, then the Axis runs theirs. Together that is one Operations Stage.
⚑ Group decision, not a printed rule.
Axis

Keep three tallies per unit

  1. CP spent this stage (resets each stage). Going over the unit's CPA costs 1 Disorganization Point (DP) per CP.
  2. Breakdown Points for vehicle units (reset each stage).
  3. Cohesion: starts at 0, drops 1 per DP, carries over between stages.
CPA rule 6.21Cohesion 6.2Breakdown 21.25
Why

Why bother tracking CP?

CP is the budget for everything: moving, firing, assaulting, even being shot at. A unit that runs out keeps acting but loses cohesion, which later hurts its morale rolls. Most of the decisions below are really CP decisions.
Allied Movement & Combat Phase
Step 3

Allied plan

Allies

Goal: take Halfaya Pass

  1. Coast group climbs the coast road to C3922, below the pass.
  2. 22nd Guards with the 4 RTR Matildas step to C3722, beside the pass on the plateau.
  3. 7th Armd Bde drives to C3721 (Sidi Suleiman) so its 4 RHA can shell the pass.
  4. Shell the Italian infantry, then assault with Guards + Matildas.
Axis waits. The Axis acts only when given a reaction window or a defensive choice.
Why

Why this plan and not another?

Halfaya is the weakest victory hex: one infantry battalion and an artillery regiment, far from the panzers.

Why 3721 and not 3820? A stack in 3820 would surround Halfaya. Defenders who cannot retreat just take a small extra loss and stay. Leaving C3921 open lets a Retreat result actually empty the hex.

Why not pin the panzers with the Hussars? To pin, the Hussars must sit next to C4019 and announce an assault. C4019 exerts a ZOC, so they would then have to attack the whole panzer reserve.

Step 7

End-of-movement checks

Allies

Ask: is any of my units in an enemy ZOC?

The Allies ask the Axis about each adjacent Axis hex. The Axis card shows how the answer is worked out. Halfaya: no ZOC. Sollum: no ZOC. So no Allied unit is forced to attack anything.
Size test 10.11Strength test 10.15Must attack 10.31
Axis

Your first ZOC check: does each of my hexes exert a ZOC?

What a ZOC is. A Zone of Control is the six hexes around a hex of your combat units. An enemy unit that enters it must stop moving (10.22). If it is still there when its Movement Segment ends, it must attack that hex or fire a Holding Off barrage at it (10.31).

When you check. Whenever an enemy unit stops next to one of your hexes, and again at the end of every enemy Movement Segment. The Allies ask, and you must answer truthfully (10.16).

A hex exerts a ZOC only if it passes both tests:
  1. Size: the combat units in the hex total more than 1 stacking point (10.11).
  2. Strength: their raw defensive Close Assault points total at least 10 (defensive CA × TOE, added up for the hex) (10.15).
One more limit: a ZOC never extends across an escarpment hexside (10.21).

Check each of your hexes next to an Allied unit:
Halfaya, C3821 (I/62 + 57th)
Size: 1 + 1 = 2 SP → more than 1 ✓
Strength: I/62 1 × 7 TOE = 7; 57th field guns defend at 0; 75/46 bracketed (1) doesn't count beside I/62 → 7
7 < 10 ✗ → no ZOC
Sollum, C4021 (II/20)
Size: 1 SP → not more than 1 ✗ → no ZOC (no need to check strength)
Fort Capuzzo, Bardia, C4019: no Allied unit adjacent → nothing to answer
Your answer to the Allies: “Neither Halfaya nor Sollum exerts a ZOC.”
ZOC 10.1110.1510.16Escarpment 10.21Stop 10.22Must attack 10.31
Why

Why this matters

Attacking Halfaya is now a choice, not an obligation. If the hex had a ZOC, every adjacent Allied stack would have to attack it or fire a Holding Off barrage.
Step 8

Breakdown rolls

Allies

Roll for every vehicle unit that moved

Where the points come from: every vehicle unit starts each Operations Stage at 0 Breakdown Points (they reset at the end of every stage, 21.25). Each hex it enters adds that terrain's Breakdown cost from the TEC: clear = 4 (along a road, ½). Nothing else adds points: firing, assaulting and being shelled don't.

So this stage: 7th Armd Bde units entered 2 clear hexes = 0 + 4 + 4 = 8 BP; 4 RTR entered 1 clear hex = 0 + 4 = 4 BP; the Coast group has no vehicle units that check.

Then find the column for the unit's points, shift it by the unit's BAR, and roll.
2 RTR (A13, 1R)⚂⚅🎲 Breakdown Table [21.38]→ 10%: 1 A13 breaks down
7 Bde HQ (A9, 1R)⚀⚃🎲 Breakdown Table [21.38]→ 0%
4 RTR (Matilda, 1R)⚁⚁🎲 Breakdown Table [21.38]→ 0%
2 RTR: 8 BP → column 4–10 → shift right → 11–20. 36 is in 33–62 = 10%. 10% × 10 TOE = 1 TOE
7 Bde HQ: same column; 14 is in 11–32 = 0%
4 RTR moved 1 hex = 4 BP (more than 3, so it checks): 4–10 → 11–20; 22 = 0%
11 Hus, 6 AusCav (1L): 4–10 shifted left falls off the table → no roll
Guns and infantry never break down
Breakdown Table [21.38]BAR: Tank & Gun chart21.27 more than 3 pointsReset 21.25TEC [8.37] Breakdown column
Axis: nothing moved, nothing to roll.
Why

Why 2 RTR now has 9 working tanks

The marker goes in C3721 and stays there. Rules-strict version: show only a number on it (“BD 1”) and keep “BD 1 = 2 RTR, 1 A13” on your sheet.
Place a numbered Broken Down Vehicle marker in C3721 and write on your Broken Down Vehicles Sheet: marker number, 2 RTR, 1 A13. The other side doesn't get to see what the marker holds. The marker stays in the hex when 2 RTR moves on. If an enemy battalion moves next to it while no friendly combat unit, HQ or engineer is stacked with it, the enemy captures it. It can't move (except by towing) or fight until repaired. The early British cruisers really were this unreliable, which is why their BAR is 1R.

Combat a: Forward or Back

Allies

Secretly set guns and armour

  • 4 RHA, 8 Fld: Forward (only Forward guns can combine fire).
  • 3 RHA, 2/3 Aus: Back: Halfaya has no tanks to shoot.
  • 4 RTR: Forward (it assaults). 2 RTR: Back.
Positions 12.13–12.16
Axis

Secretly set the 57th

Forward. It can then barrage the Guards and fire its 75/46 AA guns at the Matildas.
12.13
Why

The Forward/Back trade-off

Forward guns fight, but the defender's Forward guns also take Vulnerability losses in a Close Assault. Back guns are safe unless the assault becomes an Overrun. The 57th accepts the risk because Back guns would leave Halfaya with no way to hit back.

The pinning trick

A unit 6 or more CPA faster that announces a Close Assault freezes slower motorized enemies. Recce goes first so the Matilda stack can't slip away before the panzers arrive. This is exactly what the recce battalions are for.

Step 31

What you now know how to do

Allies

Allied lessons

  • Leave the enemy an exit, or a Retreat result does nothing.
  • Pin infantry before you assault.
  • Don't park infantry with artillery that fires.
Axis

Axis lessons

  • Recce first: it freezes slower units.
  • Pin the enemy's armour, then shoot its anti-tank guns with yours.
  • Check must-attack obligations everywhere, including quiet hexes like Sollum.
Why

Running Stage 2 yourselves

Follow the same order every time: move → reaction checks → breakdown → positions → barrage → retreat before assault → force assignment → anti-armor → close assault → retreats, keeping the three tallies (CP, Breakdown Points, Cohesion) as you go. The turn flowchart and combat pages in your PDF follow exactly this order.
